brief: The Fed held its policy rate at 3.75-4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack dissenting for a 25 bp hike, the fourth dissent favoring a hike this year after Hammack, Logan and Kashkari in July. The statement added that waiting to accumulate more information would support a timely return of inflation to target, echoing the no-urgency message from Williams, Jefferson and Waller and the September dot plot's call for one more hike by year-end rather than back-to-back increases. Chair Warsh's press conference read more dovish than expected: the statement upgraded growth language from 'solid' to 'strong,' Warsh said the economy had strengthened and that financial conditions had tightened since September, though he still would not call them tight. SEB reads this as supportive of its own call for one more hike in December, then a hold before cuts resume in late 2027, with upside risk from Middle East conflict and energy prices and downside risk from rising real yields. Balance-sheet decisions wait for a task force report in Q1. The Fed will also carve out dedicated strategy meetings starting fall 2027. Markets priced the statement as dovish: front-end yields fell and the Nasdaq rose.
